interest: Traces Japan's shift to a wartime command economy, including the new Ministry of Health and Social Affairs.
keywords: Ministry of Health and Social Affairs
overview: This file (U.S. State Department decimal file 894.02, covering November 1930 to May 1939) documents the structural reorganization of the executive departments of the Japanese government during the interwar and early wartime periods. It spans initial financial retrenchment proposals under Finance Minister Inouye in 1931, the wartime creation of Imperial General Headquarters in late 1937, the establishment of the Ministry of Health and Social Affairs (Kōseishō) to manage labor, social welfare, and military-age physical examinations, and bureaucratic infighting between the Foreign Office and the Cabinet over the administration of occupied China. It culminates in reports and the complete English translation of Imperial Ordinance No. 179 of March 1939, which reorganized the Ministry of Commerce and Industry into a permanent organ of price control and commodity adjustment and imposed strict limits on corporate dividends and capital accommodation under the National General Mobilization Law.

subfiles.about: Report on proposed administrative changes and retrenchment plans recommended by the Readjustment Commission.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes proposals by the Administrative and Financial Readjustment Commission aimed at cutting government expenditures by 100,000,000 yen. Measures include abolishing the Department of Overseas Affairs and placing colonial supervision under the Cabinet, merging Agriculture and Forestry with Commerce and Industry, and streamlining various ministerial bureaus under Finance Minister Inouye.

subfiles.about: Division analysis of Tokyo Despatch No. 3814 regarding economic mobilization and price controls.
subfiles.from: Laurence E. Salisbury (Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Memorandum summarizing Despatch No. 3814 from Tokyo, prepared by Frank Schuler, regarding the major administrative overhaul of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. Salisbury highlights the permanent institutionalization of wartime price controls and commodity supply organs, noting the Embassy's comparison of the system to German and Italian fascist models.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Reorganization of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting on the reorganization of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry under mobilization powers.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew (Tokyo; drafted by Frank A. Schuler)
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports on the structural transformation of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry to implement Articles 11 and 19 of the National General Mobilization Law. The changes make temporary emergency organs permanent by establishing an independent Price Bureau, expanding existing bureaus, and creating a Deliberative Council to coordinate military and civilian commodity demands. The despatch emphasizes conscious Japanese imitation and adaptation of German and Italian fascist economic controls.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3814 on Reorganization of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry

subfiles.about: Imperial ordinance enforcing corporate dividend restrictions and state-directed capital accommodation.
subfiles.from: Prime Minister Kiichirō Hiranuma and Cabinet Ministers
subfiles.summary: Translation of Imperial Ordinance No. 179 putting into effect Article 11 of the National General Mobilization Law. It restricts corporations capitalized at ¥200,000 or more from distributing dividends above standard fixed rates (typically 6% to 10%) without ministerial approval and establishes a Committee for Investigation of Profit Distribution. It also empowers the Minister of Finance to compel the Industrial Bank of Japan to supply industrial capital for priority production, backed by government compensation for losses.
subfiles.title: Translation of Imperial Ordinance No. 179 Concerning Distribution of Profit and Capital Accommodation
